summary: ONE target row, and the answer is that AFL IS RIGHT — ep 79 is filler, the stored type is confirmed, and this is a result, not an empty verdict. The disagreement: animefillerlist's live row 79 reads 'Filler' (2002-07-22, 'Jaken's Plan to Steal Tetsusaiga'), while animefillerguide's row 79 is blue-classed 'Mixed' with chapter 219. AFG's own note is what refutes AFG's class — it reads, verbatim: 'Mixed, all you have to see is the end of the episode, from minute 21:05 to the end .~ Netflix: 21:11 to the end . This only adapts page 1 of manga 219.' One page, in the last ~90 seconds of a 23-minute episode. Two independent sources beyond the two labels confirm the accounting exactly. (1) inuyasha.fandom's Episode 79 page: infobox 'chapter = Chapter 219 {{C|end of the episode}}', Notes section 'All of this episode but the last scene, where Kagura kidnaps Rin, is anime filler', and the page carries Category:Filler episodes; its full summary is a Jaken comedy — Jaken hires the demon Muotoko to steal Tessaiga, fails, runs a fake sword-sharpening stall, fails, conjures a hot spring to lure Inuyasha away, fails again — with the abduction only as the closing tag. (2) ja-Wikipedia's 犬夜叉 (アニメ) 各話 table carries a per-episode 原作 column in 巻話 form, and prints for 第79話 exactly '23巻1話 / TVオリジナル' — volume 23 chapter 1 IS ch 219 (the fandom's Chapter 219 page: volume=23, piece=1), so ja-WP independently says 'ch 219 is present AND the rest is TV-original'. The rows around it are the control: 75-78 are a rowspan of plain 'TVオリジナル', 80-81 are '23巻1-5話', 82 is '23巻6話'. THE TYPE, under T28 and the sliver clause: segment 1, ~21 of ~23 minutes, the Jaken plot, anime-original, no source pages; segment 2, ch 219 page 1 (Kagura abducting Rin in front of Jaken in a melon field), weight SLIVER. I ran the sole-adaptation exception and state both halves. Half (a) probably HOLDS: ep 80 does not re-stage the abduction — its summary opens with Jaken already 'rushing to Sesshōmaru's side to tell him that Rin was abducted by Kagura', i.e. after the fact, so the panel itself is likely sole to ep 79 (the fandom's Chapter 219 page lists BOTH Episode 79 and Episode 80, and ja-WP credits 23巻1話 to both, so the chapter is shared, the page probably not). Half (b) FAILS: Rin's abduction is a one-page setup transition that launches the next two episodes, not 'a death, a reveal, an arc close' — and its content is verbally restated in ep 80's first minute, so nothing about the source is lost by typing 79 filler. One half is not two: the fragment is a graft on an original plot, so the row stays FILLER (T28) and takes no anchor (A1). Ch 219 is not stranded — ep 80's stored anchor is START 219, {219-221}, and it adapts the chapter properly. Which source lied: animefillerguide, twice over — its blue 'Mixed' CLASS overstates a single page into a co-equal standing, and its chapter column then prints '219' on rows 79 AND 80 without partitioning, the reading-position-header shape. Its own prose is the disproof, which is the useful lesson: on AFG, read the note before the class. The stored 'partial {219 (opening beat)}' annotation is factually right but its wording is not: it says the beat was 're-staged in a melon field', implying an anime invention, when the melon field is the MANGA's own setting (ch 219: 'While stealing food, Rin is visited by Kagura who kidnaps her, in front of Jaken', and the melon reappears in ep 80 when Rin shares it with Kohaku). Corrected annotation below, kind changed partial → graft, with the weight and the episode that adapts ch 219 properly named.

anchor_hostile.why: A1: the row is filler (confirmed, not merely stored) — ~21 of ~23 minutes are an anime-original Jaken comedy with no source pages, and the only source material is ch 219 page 1 in the closing tag, weight SLIVER. A44 independently: a single first-time page inside an original plot is a position-less fragment; ch 219 is properly adapted by ep 80, whose stored anchor already carries START 219 / {219-221}, so no position is lost by declining the anchor here and no chapter is marked never-adapted. Sean's 2026-08-25 A1 deletion on this row ('wholly anime-original Jaken comedy episode') is CONFIRMED by this research, not re-opened.

annotations.note: weight: SLIVER — because it is one page (animefillerguide states it outright: 'This only adapts page 1 of manga 219'), it runs from 21:05 to the end of a ~23-minute episode whose other ~21 minutes have no source pages, and it is a setup transition rather than a story-carrying share of this episode's own plot (the episode's job is the Jaken/Tessaiga comedy). The material is NEW rather than a duplicate — ep 80 opens after the abduction, with Jaken already reporting it to Sesshōmaru — but ch 219 is adapted PROPERLY by ep 80, which carries the anchor (START 219, {219-221}); read the chapter there. Sole-adaptation exception checked and DECLINED: half (a) holds (the panel is likely in no other episode), half (b) fails (a one-page abduction that opens a chapter is not a death, a reveal or an arc close, and ep 80 restates the event in its first minute). Both halves are required. Note also that this beat is FAITHFUL, not restaged: the melon field is the manga's own setting (ch 219 opens with Rin stealing food; ep 80 has her sharing that melon with Kohaku) — the stored annotation's 're-staged in a melon field' wording should be dropped. Replaces the stored partial{219 (opening beat)} fact; kind corrected partial → graft, since the episode does not partially adapt a chapter it is otherwise adapting, it quotes one page of a chapter that belongs to the next episode.

structure.notes: STORED TYPE CONFIRMED — no type_correction, deliberately: ep 79 stays filler, and AFL is the label that got it right. Row identity checked before any join: AFL's inuyasha page holds 194 rows against our 193, so nothing was index-joined; row 79 was matched on TITLE + DATE ('Jaken's Plan to Steal Tetsusaiga', 2002-07-22) and rows 76-83 were read around it to confirm the block boundary (75-78 Filler, 79 Filler, 80-82 Manga Canon, 83 Mixed Canon/Filler) — that boundary matches ja-WP's 原作 column and our stored types exactly, which is the strongest available evidence that the two lists are aligned here. AFG's inuyasha table is 193 data rows and joins by title. THE FIND WORTH KEEPING: ja-Wikipedia's 犬夜叉 (アニメ) article carries a per-episode 原作 column in 巻話 form for the whole TV run — 第79話 '23巻1話 / TVオリジナル', 第80-81話 '23巻1-5話' (rowspan), 第82話 '23巻6話', 第83-84話 'TVオリジナル / 23巻7-9話' (rowspan), 第75-78話 'TVオリジナル' (rowspan). This is the ja-WP per-episode instrument the catalog already prizes on other series, and InuYasha HAS it — the context file records 'Volume boundaries (0) none' and 136 afg-tier anchors, so this column is an unexploited independent leg for the whole series, not just this row. Chapter space: one space — the fandom's Chapter 219 page reads volume=23, piece=1, and vol 23 chapter 1 = ch 219 under the 558-chapter / 56-volume numbering AniList and our anchors use; ja-WP's 巻話 pairs convert into it cleanly at three independent boundaries checked (23巻1話=219, 23巻6話=224 which sits inside ep 82's stored {223-224}, 22巻6-10話=eps 73-74 which sits inside the stored ep-74 {215-218}). Note the small residual: ja-WP gives ep 82 '23巻6話' = ch 224 while our stored ep-82 anchor is {223-224} — consistent, the anime straddles. No repair proposed. Sources beyond the two labels: (1) inuyasha.fandom via the MediaWiki API — Episode 79 (infobox chapter field, Notes, Category:Filler episodes, full summary), Episode 80 (summary + chapter=219-221), Chapter 219 and Chapter 218 pages; (2) ja-Wikipedia 犬夜叉 (アニメ), 各話 table with its 原作 column. Both read as raw wikitext.
structure.coverage_set_checked: ep 74 {215-218}, eps 75-78 all-original (ja-WP TVオリジナル, AFL Filler, AFG 'N/A *Filler' red), ep 79 = ch 219 p.1 only, ep 80 {219-221}, ep 81 {221-223}, ep 82 {223-224} — ch 219's number is fully owned by ep 80.

flags_for_sean: AFL confirmed, AFG refuted — and the mechanism is a trap worth adding to the agent definition: animefillerguide's blue 'Mixed' class can rest on a single page, and AFG SAYS SO in the same cell. Row 79's text is 'Mixed, all you have to see is the end of the episode, from minute 21:05 to the end .~ Netflix: 21:11 to the end . This only adapts page 1 of manga 219.' On this source, the note is evidence and the class is an opinion; read the note first. The same cell shape produced the slam-dunk 92 flag in this same wave ('Mixed, in this episode we only watch from minute 19:14 to the end'), so it is a systematic AFG behaviour, not a one-off.

A real find beyond the ask: ja-Wikipedia's 犬夜叉 (アニメ) article has a per-episode 原作 column in 巻話 form covering the whole 167-episode TV run, with explicit TVオリジナル rows and rowspans. Our 136 InuYasha anchors below ep 167 are ALL afg-tier (derivation), and this column is a genuinely independent second leg for every one of them — including the several stored rows whose chapters_adapted look odd (ep 13 {24, 39-44}, ep 152 {304, 311-313}). Worth a lane of its own; I did not touch anything outside ep 79.

The stored annotation on ep 79 says the beat was 're-staged in a melon field after the anime-original Jaken plot'. That is wrong in a small way: the melon field is the MANGA's setting (ch 219 opens with Rin stealing food and ep 80 has her sharing that melon with Kohaku), so the tag is a faithful animation of the page, not a restaging. The corrected annotation is in this verdict; the type is unaffected either way.

Half (a) of the sole-adaptation exception is PROBABLE rather than proven here: I established that ep 80's summary begins after the abduction, but no source states page-for-page that ep 80 never shows the kidnapping panel. It does not change the outcome — half (b) fails on its own, and both halves are required — but if you ever want the page-level fact, the missing instrument is a per-episode Japanese synopsis (Yomiuri TV / Sunrise), which I could not find archived for 2002.
